question: A development team is designing an internal agent that must autonomously read repository files, run shell commands, and edit code without the team writing their own tool-execution loop. Which design choice fits this requirement?
options: A) Call the Messages API once per file and manually stitch together the results without any tool-execution loop
B) Use the Usage and Cost Admin API to orchestrate tool calls across the repository on the team's behalf
C) Build on the Anthropic Client SDK and implement a loop that inspects each response's stop reason and executes tools manually
D) Build on the Claude Agent SDK, which provides the built-in tools, agent loop, and context management out of the box
correct_answers: D) Build on the Claude Agent SDK, which provides the built-in tools, agent loop, and context management out of the box
explanations: Calling the Messages API once per file without a tool loop cannot autonomously read files, run commands, or edit code as required.
The Usage and Cost Admin API reports token usage and spend; it has no role in executing tools or orchestrating an agent.
The Client SDK gives direct API access, but the team would still need to implement the tool loop themselves, which the requirement explicitly avoids.
Correct - the Agent SDK ships with built-in tools, the agent loop, and context management so the team does not implement tool execution from scratch.
